This appeal coming on for admission this day, 
 following:
 ORDER Heard finally with the consent of learned counsel for the parties.

2. This Misc. Appeal has been filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act,1988 against the award dated 3/8/2022 passed in Claim Case No.69/2021.
3.

Since only limited point of income and deduction in the head of personal expenses has been challenged in this appeal for enhancement of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17739 the compensation amount, therefore, vivid description of all the facts relating to the accident is not given.

4. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that deceased Ashish Kushwaha, who died in motor accident on 1/6/2020, his legal heirs ; wife Maya Kushwaha, a minor daughter Kumari Shivangi and one minor son Om Kushwaha had filed a claim petition and now they are appellants before this court.

Learned claims tribunal has assessed income of the deceased as Rs.7700/- p.m. whereas according to the circular issued by the Labour Department for minimum wages effective on the date of the death of the deceased, minimum wages for the un-skilled labourers was fixed Rs.8275/- p.m.

Since the appellants/legal heirs of the deceased are three in numbers, therefore, as per paragraph 32 of the judgment of the Apex Court passed in the case of Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation (2009) 6 SCC 121, deduction in the head of personal expenses should have been taken as 1/3rd whereas the learned claims tribunal has deducted 50% of the amount in personal expenses which is erroneous and on this grounds, learned counsel for the appellants prays for enhancing the award amount.

Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent no.3/insurance company supports the award and prays for dismissing the appeal.

6. It is not in dispute that the deceased had no fixed income, therefore, his income should have been assessed as per circular prevailing on the date of death issued under the Minimum Wages Act by the Labour Department.
As per circular effective on the date of death, in the instant case, income of the unskilled labourer has been fixed to Rs.8,275/- p.m.
Thus, the learned claims tribunal has committed error in assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.7700/- p.m. only.

Thus, income of the deceased is assessed to Rs.8275/-.
7.

As far as deduction in the head of personal expenses is concerned looking to the number of the legal heirs of the deceased, as per directions given by the Apex Court in the paragraph 32 of Sarla Verma's case (Supra), only 1/3rd amount should have been deducted in the head of personal expenses.
Learned claims tribunal has committed error in deducting  in the above head.
While computing the award amount,  will be deducted in the head of personal expenses.

Accordingly, appellants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.1,68,500/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
